title: How Bees Share Directions
subject: bio
paras: Honeybees live in large colonies, and most of the bees in a hive spend their days collecting food. A single colony may need nectar from millions of flowers to survive the winter. Because good patches of flowers can be far from the hive, bees need a way to tell one another where food can be found.

In the 1940s, the Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch discovered that bees communicate through movement. When a forager returns from a rich source of nectar, she performs a pattern of steps on the wall of the hive. Von Frisch called this pattern the waggle dance. During the dance, the bee runs in a straight line while shaking her body from side to side, then circles back and repeats the run.

The dance carries two kinds of information. First, the angle of the straight run shows direction. If the bee runs straight up the wall, the food lies in the same direction as the sun. If she runs at an angle to the right of vertical, the food lies at that same angle to the right of the sun. Second, the length of the run shows distance: the longer the waggle, the farther away the flowers are.

Other bees gather around the dancer and follow her closely. They also learn the scent of the flowers from her body. Then they fly out and search the area she has described. Experiments in which scientists moved feeding stations to new places showed that recruits flew in the right direction even when they could not see or smell the food from the hive.

The waggle dance is one of the few known examples of an animal communicating about something that is not present. For this reason, it remains one of the most studied behaviors in biology, and von Frisch received a Nobel Prize for his work in 1973.

qs.q: According to paragraph 1, why do honeybees need a way to communicate about food?
opts: Each bee can only visit a few flowers a day.
Rich patches of flowers may be far from the hive.
Flowers produce nectar only in winter.
The queen must approve every trip.
qs.why: 第1段：Because good patches of flowers can be far from the hive, bees need a way to tell one another…

qs.q: The word "forager" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
opts: a guard
a food collector
a young bee
a builder
qs.why: forager 指外出觅食者，上文 collecting food 也有提示。

qs.q: According to paragraph 3, what does the length of the waggle run indicate?
opts: The direction of the sun
The amount of nectar
How far away the food is
How many bees should go
qs.why: the longer the waggle, the farther away the flowers are.

qs.q: What can be inferred from paragraph 3 about a bee that runs straight down the wall?
opts: The food is in the direction opposite the sun.
The food is very close to the hive.
There is no food nearby.
The sun has already set.
qs.why: 向上=朝太阳方向，那么向下就是背对太阳的方向。

qs.q: Why does the author mention experiments with moved feeding stations in paragraph 4?
opts: To show that bees prefer new flowers
To explain how scent travels
To provide evidence that the dance itself carries location information
To argue that von Frisch's ideas were wrong
qs.why: 实验说明即使看不见、闻不到，新蜂也能飞对方向——信息来自舞蹈。

qs.q: According to the passage, all of the following are true of the waggle dance EXCEPT:
opts: It shows direction relative to the sun.
Other bees learn the flowers' scent from the dancer.
It was first described in the 1940s.
It is performed outside the hive.
qs.why: 第2段说舞蹈在蜂巢内壁上跳（on the wall of the hive）。
